layout_summary: An asymmetric poster on pure white: a red patent stiletto enters from the left edge in the upper-left area, and its heel melts into a three-pronged devil's fork that drips into a jar of caramel spread in the lower-left. A movie-title serif lockup sits in the right half, roughly level with the heel and the fork, and one centred line of red rounded-sans copy runs across the foot of the canvas.

DEVIL and BISCOFF share a left edge at x≈46.5% and a right edge at x≈90–91%
The red word THE is set off-centre, its left edge at x≈52% (over the 'E' of DEVIL), echoing the film-logo lockup
The tagline is centred on the canvas axis at x=50%
The drip and fork centre-line (x≈24.5%) sits about at the jar's centre-line (x≈24.5%), so the shoe-to-jar flow is one vertical axis
The top of the title (y≈31%) roughly lines up with the point where the heel leaves the shoe body (y≈31–34%)

scene.subject: A glossy red patent stiletto pump seen in side profile. Its stiletto heel turns into a thin stream of liquid red that ends in a three-pronged devil's pitchfork. The fork's tines are dipped into the top of a glass jar of smooth caramel-brown spread, and spread overflows the lid and runs down the jar's sides. The jar has a red wrap-around label with a speculoos-biscuit illustration on its right side. A soft contact shadow sits under the jar.
scene.composition: The shoe enters from the left edge. Its toe is cropped off-canvas at x=0, y≈42–52%, and it rises diagonally up and right to the heel counter, whose highest point is at x≈29%, y≈10%. The heel cup's rightmost point is at x≈36%, y≈25%. The heel drips straight down as a thin stem from y≈34% to the fork at y≈48–55%, with the fork centred at x≈24.5% and about 8% wide. The jar sits upright from x≈14.5–35%, y≈55.5–82.5%, about 20% of the canvas wide. Everything sits in the left 36% of the frame.
scene.camera: Straight side-on, eye-level product view. Long-lens, almost orthographic feel with no perspective distortion. Everything is in sharp focus.
scene.lighting: Soft, bright studio light from the upper left. Strong specular highlights run along the patent shoe and the glossy caramel. There is a gentle shadow under the jar and none on the background, which stays a clean white.

font.family_guess: Times New Roman small caps (Bodoni-leaning transitional serif)

elements.text: Don’t be silly Andrea, everybody wants this.

ornaments.description: A thin black devil's-tail arrow in the title lockup. It replaces the right stroke of the 'V' in DEVIL, rising from the V's base up and right, past the cap line, to a solid triangular arrowhead. It is the same weight as the hairline serif strokes.

why_it_works: One visual idea with no extra steps: the shoe's heel becomes the devil's fork, which dips into the jar. The movie parody and the product link up in one look, and the title confirms it.

Strict figure/ground: saturated red-and-caramel objects on pure white, with the black serif title opposite them. The left-object/right-type split leaves big calm white fields, so the eye moves from the shoe to the title to the line at the bottom.

The type follows the parody exactly: film-logo serif with red small words, and the brand's own rounded sans for the spoken punchline. The quote borrows the film's voice, so the copy feels familiar right away.
